final_message:
Subject: On Doing Every Task Well

Dear Colleague,

I want to write you a few words about a lesson that I have been learning slowly, and which I think you will find worth considering as we begin the new quarter.

It is this: that no task is so small that it does not deserve our best effort. We are all of us inclined, I fear, to divide our work into two classes--the important and the unimportant--and to give our full strength only to the first. But I have found that this is a mistake, and a costly one. The man or woman who will do the small thing carelessly will, sooner or later, do the large thing carelessly also. Habit is not a thing that we can put on and off like a coat.

Take, for example, the matter of the weekly report. It is a small matter. Nobody will praise you for having done it well, and very few will notice if you have done it poorly. Yet I have observed that those who put their conscience into even this simple duty are the very ones to whom we turn when a difficult and important piece of work must be done. They have earned our confidence, not by one great act, but by a hundred small ones that nobody saw.

Let us remember, also, that the small task is very often the foundation upon which the large one rests. A figure that is wrongly copied, a letter that is carelessly worded, a promise that is forgotten because it seemed too trivial to write down--any one of these may undo the labor of many weeks. We cannot afford to be careless anywhere, because we cannot always tell beforehand where the carelessness will do its harm.

I do not say this because I think that you are lacking in this respect. On the contrary, I have noticed with real pleasure the care that you give to your work, and I hope that you will keep it up. But I think that it is well for each of us, now and then, to stop and to ask ourselves whether there is any department of our work in which we have allowed ourselves to grow careless or indifferent.

Let us make up our minds, then, that whatever we put our hand to--whether it be great or small, whether it be seen or unseen--we shall do it as well as it can be done. In this way we shall add to our own strength of character, and we shall also help to build up an institution of which we may be proud.

With sincere regard,

[name]
